name: Sunspot
desc: A sunspot held under an observatory's white-light plate — the photosphere boiling everywhere in granules that brighten, shoulder their neighbours aside and are replaced, until a rope of field throttles the convection and the gas there cools and goes dark: a stippled umbra split by a light bridge, ringed by penumbral filaments that each carry a dark core down their length while the Evershed flow runs brightness out along them; also a crimson H-alpha spot trailing superpenumbral fibrils, a signed magnetogram where the light is gone and only the field remains, a heliograph engraving, or ironbow thermal.

energy.doc: activity — granulation contrast, penumbral dark-core depth, Evershed speed, umbral-dot rate and the spot's own size (the master knob)

scale.doc: spot size against granule size — from a pore lost in a fine boiling field to a monster whose penumbra runs off the plate

speed.doc: time rate (0.15 still boils and still flows outward, just at the pace the real sun does it)

density.doc: granule count and penumbral filament count together — coarse supergranular cells and a few fat filaments, or a fine seething carpet combed by a hundred fine ones

tilt.doc: how far from disk centre — foreshortens the spot into an ellipse and drags the limb-darkening across the plate

bridge.doc: light bridge — a lane of surviving convection cutting the umbra in two; 0 leaves the umbra whole and black

hue.doc: plate tone (34 = the amber of a white-light solar plate); ignored by the magnetogram style, which has no colour on purpose

style.doc: aesthetic: amber white-light observatory plate / deep-crimson H-alpha chromosphere with superpenumbral fibrils streaming far past the spot / abstracted signed magnetogram — no light at all, just the field, quiet sun neutral grey and churning with network flux elements / 19th-century heliograph engraving whose burin runs radial inside the spot and cross-hatched outside / ironbow thermal false-colour

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the granule field, filament phases, umbral dots and the spot's polarity
